summary: Find cross-cutting deep-dive candidates the category sweep missed

result.title: channels
result.dek: Messaging channels as runtime capabilities: credentials live host-side, adapters self-configure off env, and unknown senders are parked behind a pairing-code allowlist before anything reaches the inbox.
result.evidence: runtime/host/channels.ex (registry + dispatch + DM pairing policy, JSON/JSONL state under WB_DATA/channels/), runtime/host/channels/telegram.ex (official Bot API adapter, supervised long-poll GenServer, configured?/0 gating in Workbooks.Application)

result.title: secrets
result.dek: The host holds the credential, the guest never sees it: sign-only secret use across the membrane, per-tenant scoping, mid-flight revocation, and plugin auth that resolves keys the plugin can't read.
result.evidence: runtime/host/secret_broker.ex (NO-READ sign/3-only broker), runtime/host/secret.ex, runtime/host/plugin/auth.ex (ENV_KEYS bearer resolution), runtime/host/vars.ex, runtime/host/revocation.ex (ETS revoke set consulted on every brokered op)

result.title: browsing
result.dek: The runtime's web capability: a free native browser by default, with fetch/crawl/search each routable to a swappable provider (Firecrawl, Exa, proxies) via config — no caller ever changes.
result.evidence: runtime/host/browse.ex (capability dispatcher), runtime/host/browse/provider.ex, native.ex, fetch.ex (127 LOC), crawl.ex, search.ex (152 LOC), extract.ex (151 LOC), firecrawl.ex

result.title: vectors
result.dek: The tenant-scoped semantic index: pure-Elixir Model2Vec embeddings (no model runtime, just vocab + matrix + mean-pool), machine-probed embedding tiers, and one store interface over brute-force SQLite or pgvector ANN.
result.evidence: runtime/host/vector.ex (backend-aware store, cosine vs <=> ), runtime/host/embed/model2vec.ex (static embeddings in :persistent_term), runtime/host/embed/capability.ex (tier probe: big_multimodal/clip/model2vec), runtime/docs/VECTOR-QUERY.org

result.title: postures
result.dek: Every workbook route has a security stance — public, gated_data, or gated_route — and the anti-leak invariant that decides what may be baked into a static file versus served only behind the auth ladder.
result.evidence: runtime/host/access.ex (three postures + enforce, the anti-leak invariant), runtime/host/auth.ex (five-rung auth ladder: allowlist, desktop token, WB_PUBLIC_BEARER, Guardian JWT, dev header)

result.title: escrow
result.dek: Gated bundle bytes are noise without a key release: content keys are escrowed runtime-side behind posture checks, or sealed-box wrapped to recipient X25519 identities so no plaintext-key honeypot ever exists.
result.evidence: runtime/host/bundle/escrow.ex (runtime-held key store, release over POST /rcp/key/:key_id after Access.enforce), runtime/host/bundle/key_wrap.ex (ephemeral ECDH → KEK → AES-256-GCM wrap), runtime/host/bundle/sealed.ex, runtime/host/did/x25519.ex (did:key Ed25519→X25519 linkage)

result.title: commands
result.dek: A command is a CLI converted to sandboxed WASM — stdin in, stdout out, invoked by name through the Dock — and guests exec each other's commands only through a default-deny broker with structural argv and bounded nesting.
result.evidence: runtime/host/command_registry.ex (1048 LOC: 32+ wasm commands, jq/grep/oql built-ins, command-vs-toolkit relationship), runtime/host/exec_broker.ex (default-deny, per-instance command allowlist, no shell-string injection, depth-limited nesting, audited denials)

result.title: the-ledger
result.dek: From editable step logs to tamper-evident provenance: every agent run's _steps.jsonl is hash-chained over raw bytes and the head is signed with the tenant's Ed25519 did:key, making runs verifiable and attributable.
result.evidence: runtime/host/ledger.ex (seal/2 hash-chain h_i = sha256(h_{i-1} || raw_line_i), verify/1, Ed25519 head signing), runtime/host/did/x25519.ex, runtime/host/git.ex (tenant did:key material)

result.title: Secrets
result.dek: Secrets-by-reference: variables marked secret are ref-only — agents substitute {{secret:KEY}} placeholders, the host injects real values only at egress, and the deploy kit stages declared secret names per deployment and delivers values through provider hooks without ever baking them into images or config.
result.evidence: runtime/host/vars.ex (ref-only model, :guest vs :host resolution, docs/SECRETS.org rule); cli/src/local.rs:445-504 (wbx var set --secret, {{var:}}/{{secret:}} refs, masked list); cli/src/deploy/mod.rs:17-21,185-274 (#+DEPLOY_SECRETS declared names, staged 0600 secrets.env, secrets set/list/unset/push); cli/deploy-kit/providers/_recipe.sh:25-46 (WB_SECRET_KEYS forwarding); cli/deploy-kit/providers/fly/bootstrap.sh:39-42 (provider_set_secrets hook)

result.title: Publishing
result.dek: Publish is distribution, not deploy: publish.org declares a surface (cloudflare-pages, gh-pages, self-hosted) with init/validate/apply convergence, ships only ASSEMBLED workbooks (bundle first), prints custom-domain URLs via PUBLISH_DOMAIN, and stays a separate axis from standing up the engine.
result.evidence: cli/src/local.rs:336-443 (publish.org template, three targets, PUBLISH_DOMAIN, shippable_html bundle-first guard, wrangler/git/HTTP PUT paths); cli/TAXONOMY.md §3+§5 (publish vs deploy collision resolved, lifecycle spine); runtime/host/publish.ex + runtime/host/publish/config.ex (runtime-side counterpart)

result.title: Recipes
result.dek: Bring-your-own-cloud without a recompile: a provider is a bootstrap.sh that sources the neutral recipe spine and fills five hooks (ensure_app, set_secrets, attach_volume, deploy_image, public_url) plus the lifecycle trio; recipes resolve from WB_PROVIDERS_DIR, the repo, or copies embedded in the binary — fly is just the bundled one.
result.evidence: cli/deploy-kit/providers/_recipe.sh (hook spine, wb_recipe_run dispatch, WB_ENGINE_ENV assembly); cli/deploy-kit/providers/fly/bootstrap.sh (full hook implementation, prebuilt vs app-build image strategies, synthesized fly.toml); cli/src/deploy/mod.rs:78-80,276-354 (include_str! embedded recipes, resolve_providers_dir chain, env -i hermetic spawn)

result.title: Distribution
result.dek: One static binary, three install lanes: a GitHub Release tagged wbx-v* feeds curl installs, an npm launcher whose postinstall downloads the matching platform asset (with PATH-shadow detection and loud failure banners), and wbx upgrade self-swaps the binary in place — plus a wb.wasm target published for in-sandbox agents.
result.evidence: cli/npm/install.js (asset resolution, redirect-following download, findShadow PATH check, non-fatal failure banner); cli/src/local.rs:585-634 (upgrade: release discovery, npm-install detection, atomic binary swap); cli/SPEC.md Distribution section (curl + npm optionalDependencies + wasm lanes); cli/npm/bin/wbx.js

result.title: Backends
result.dek: The deploy-kit one-screen config: identical runtime code, swappable storage — blob store as local filesystem or any S3/R2 endpoint, structured data as SQLite or any Postgres URL (which also flips vector search from brute-force to pgvector ANN), with every operation tenant-scoped above the backend so swapping can never widen access.
result.evidence: cli/deploy-kit/storage.env.example (the full knob surface: WB_STORAGE, WB_S3_*, WB_DATABASE_URL, WB_EMBED); runtime/host/storage.ex + runtime/host/storage/local.ex + runtime/host/storage/s3.ex (the adapter seam); runtime/host/db.ex + runtime/host/vector.ex (SQLite↔Postgres + vector backend switch)

result.title: Tokens
result.dek: Credentials with a no-rotation discipline: first cloud apply generates a 256-bit WB_PUBLIC_BEARER once and persists it (rotation would 401 every live client), clients present it as WB_ENGINE_TOKEN, and WB_SIGNING_KEY pins a stable DID across redeploys so prior signatures and ledgers keep verifying.
result.evidence: cli/src/deploy/mod.rs:374-429 (ensure_cloud_bearer idempotent generation, OsRng token, persisted-in-secrets.env notice) + TEMPLATE_FLY security block (lines 570-587); runtime/host/auth.ex (WB_PUBLIC_BEARER enforcement); cli/deploy-kit/providers/_recipe.sh:27-32 (generated secrets persisted, never rotated per-apply); cli/deploy-kit/storage.env.example:10-16 (WB_SIGNING_KEY stable-DID requirement)

result.title: crews
result.dek: Run a multi-agent keeper from one declared org manifest: a worker per member with its own def, lifecycle, and namespaced state — staggered boots, a global concurrency gate that queues runs, and board claims as a def-level protocol the runtime deliberately does not enforce.
result.evidence: runtime/host/keeper/crew.ex (manifest format, stagger, WB_CREW_MAX_CONCURRENT, board-claims doctrine), runtime/host/keeper/crew/gate.ex, examples/bit-ml/agents/crew.org + writer.org/editor.org/researcher.org/desk.org, examples/bit-ml/board/pipeline.org, crew shape in runtime/host/public_web.ex (wb-wc0.2 {agents, wire} feed)

result.title: residents
result.dek: The resident pattern proven on workbooks.sh itself: a team-built page that hosts one agent inside its own repo, on a cadence, with explicit territory — the people own the shell, the resident grows designated regions through a build lane and a no-build runtime-CMS lane, one verified change per run.
result.evidence: examples/living-lander/agent/agent.org (def, cadence, territory + HANDS OFF zones, authoring lanes), examples/living-lander/app/WALDO.md (the runtime-CMS lane: sections.json manifest + content partials), examples/README.md (fleet table framing each example as app + resident agents)

result.title: archetypes
result.dek: How agent-authored UI stays designed instead of generic: a catalog of section shapes — each with a job, an earn-its-place gate, a fixed composition, and named motion signatures — plus a non-advisory taste gate every run must pass before a section ships.
result.evidence: examples/living-lander/app/SECTION-ARCHETYPES.md (catalog, foundation primitives, the eight motion signatures), examples/living-lander/agent/design-gate.org (the taste gate: PASS or it does not ship), examples/living-lander/agent/design.org, examples/living-lander/app/src/lib (ui primitives + motion.js the skeletons compose)

result.title: rehearsals
result.dek: Self-demos for agents whose last hop can't be CI: drive the real persona and real tools through the production bridge with scripted human lines and no external service, writing a transcript that proves the whole conversation layer end-to-end.
result.evidence: runtime/host/groundskeeper/rehearsal.ex (persona from the def, every tool call through the real /gk router via Plug.Test, transcript writer), examples/groundwork/rehearsals/2026-06-11-045937.org (a real rehearsal transcript), examples/groundwork/README.md (rehearsals as a first-class directory of the method)

result.title: dispatch
result.dek: A conversational agent that hands work to background workflows and hears back: an authored org workflow per request, a supervised time-bounded run bound to a task ledger, completions queued as feedback the agent drains on its next turn, and a git-visible TASKS.org rendered from the runtime — never hand-edited.
result.evidence: runtime/host/groundskeeper/tasks.ex (ledger GenServer, run_async supervision + 35-min bound, drain_feedback loop, orphan reset), runtime/host/groundskeeper/board.ex, examples/groundwork/workflows/research-e2b-e2b-dev-and-daytona-daytona-3.org (a persisted Mercury-authored workflow), examples/groundwork/TASKS.org

result.title: claims
result.dek: Turn raw founder talk into an auditable working document: every load-bearing claim extracted as an org TODO item with an honesty status (CLAIMED → VALIDATING → KEPT/PARTIAL/UNKEPT/FUTURE/RETRACTED), every terminal status citing evidence — the gap between the spoken system and the shipped system becomes the backlog.
result.evidence: examples/groundwork/audits/spoken-thesis.org (the custom #+TODO keyword ladder, quote+evidence per claim, 91-min source audited), examples/groundwork/README.md (the recording → verbatim → claims → backlog pipeline), examples/groundwork/sources/ (untouched verbatim inputs the audit points back to)

result.title: changelogs
result.dek: Published apps serve their own history: an anonymous read-only /_changes feed (git log + agent status, public-plane rules) that the page itself consumes — classifying who made each commit, collapsing quiet human groups, and narrating the work live so visitors watch people and agents build together.
result.evidence: runtime/host/public_web.ex (get /_changes — git log_entries + keeper status, singleton vs crew shapes, plane rules), examples/living-lander/app/src/lib/stores.js (the watch() loop, classify()/describeCommit, one-engine feed subscribers, raw.githubusercontent mirror reads), runtime/host/git.ex
